h: Pinetum, Castles and a Hilltop Village
p: Bedgebury rewards people who give it the whole day rather than squeezing the ropes in between other plans. The treetop course itself takes a good couple of hours once you count the briefing, and most folk come down hungry, buzzing and keen to tell everyone which crossing nearly beat them. Build in time for a sit-down and a proper wander afterwards and you'll get far more out of the trip.

If you've got non-climbers in the party, the forest is generous to them too. The Pinetum paths are wide and easy-going, and there's something calming about strolling among trees gathered from all over the world while the braver lot are swinging about overhead.

A few first-timer tips: use your legs more than your arms on the climbs, keep your phone in a zipped pocket if you want photos, and don't look down until you're ready to. Gloves are handy if your hands aren't used to rope.

The surrounding corner of the Weald is a cracking one to explore. Goudhurst itself sits on a hill with a church at the top and views that roll out for miles across orchards and oast houses. Scotney Castle, the National Trust estate near Lamberhurst with its moated ruin and romantic gardens, is a short drive away, and Bewl Water is close by for a lakeside walk. Sissinghurst's famous gardens are within reach too, if anyone in the group fancies something gentler for day two.
